'''Olabisi Oreofe Ugbebor'''  (born Grace Olabisi Falode, 29 January 1951)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sci.ui.edu.ng/OOUgbebor|title=Professor O.O. Ugbebor|work=Faculty of Science|publisher=University of Ibadan|access-date=2017-03-21}}</ref> is the first female professor in mathematics in [[Nigeria]].<ref name="queen">{{Cite news|url=http://thenationonlineng.net/meet-nigerias-queen-of-mathematics/|location=Lagos, Nigeria|title=Meet Nigeria's queen of Mathematics|date=2013-07-21|access-date=2017-03-21|language=en-US|newspaper=[[The Nation (Nigeria)|The Nation]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FAgfAQAAIAAJ|title=Perspectives on women in science and technology in Nigeria|last=Erinosho|first=Stella Yemisi|date=1994-01-01|publisher=Sam Bookman|isbn=9789782165374 |language=en}}</ref> Born in [[Lagos]], she studied mathematics at the [[University of Ibadan]] and then at the [[University of London]], where she obtained a PhD in 1976.<ref name="queen"/><ref name="mg">{{mathgenealogy|id=190629}}</ref>

== Education and academic career ==
Born in Lagos, Ugbebor had her secondary education at [[Queen's College, Lagos]]. She completed her first degree in mathematics from [[University of Ibadan]] in 1972. In 1973, she had a postgraduate diploma in statistics at [[University College London]], before completing her thesis on ''Sample Path Properties of [[Brownian Motion]]'' (1976) at the age of 25. While at Unibadan, she was the only female student in her class. She is also the first Nigerian woman to get a PhD and become a professor in mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.fab.ng/2017/09/first-nigerian-woman-obtain-ph-d-degree-mathematics/ |title=Meet Professor Olabisi Ugbebor, First Nigerian Woman To Obtain A Ph.D. Degree In Mathematics |website=fab.ng |access-date=2018-02-18 |date=2017-09-30 |archive-date=2018-05-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180523010142/http://www.fab.ng/2017/09/first-nigerian-woman-obtain-ph-d-degree-mathematics/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2017, she was made a Fellow of the Mathematics Association of Nigeria.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.vanguardngr.com/2017/08/adeboye-3-women-mathematicians-bag-highest-award/ |location=Lagos, Nigeria|title=Adeboye, 3 women mathematicians bag highest award  |newspaper=[[Vanguard (Nigeria)|Vanguard]]|access-date=2018-02-18|date=2017-08-26 }}</ref>
